If you flew close to the speed of light for one year, you'd come home to find your twin brother ten years older.
In 1971, scientists flew super precise atomic clocks around the world on ordinary passenger jets.
When they landed, the clocks no longer matched the ones left on the ground.
And it is happening above your head right now. GPS satellite clocks gain 38 millionths of a second every day, and without fixing it, your map would drift about ten kilometres daily.
Einstein showed that time is not fixed. The faster you move, the slower your clock ticks. At ninety nine point five percent of light speed, one of your years equals ten on Earth.
So the fastest traveller would not just leave home. They would come back to a world where everyone they loved grew old without them.
